In [[matrix analysis]] '''Stahl's theorem''' is a theorem proved in 2011 by [[Herbert Robert Stahl|Herbert Stahl]] concerning Laplace transforms for special matrix functions.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Stahl, Herbert R.|title=Proof of the BMV conjecture|journal=Acta Mathematica|volume=211|issue=2|year=2013|pages=255–290|doi=10.1007/s11511-013-0104-z |arxiv=1107.4875}}</ref> It originated in 1975 as the Bessis-Moussa-Villani (BMV) conjecture by Daniel Bessis, Pierre Moussa, and Marcel Villani.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bessis, D.|author2=Moussa, P.|author3=Villani, M.|title=Monotonic converging variational approximations to the functional integrals in quantum statistical mechanics|journal= Journal of Mathematical Physics|volume=16|issue=11|pages=2318–2325|year=1975|doi=10.1063/1.522463|bibcode=1975JMP....16.2318B|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2004 [[Elliott H. Lieb]] and [[Robert Seiringer]] gave two important reformulations of the BMV conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Lieb, Elliott|author2=Seiringer, Robert|title=Equivalent forms of the Bessis-Moussa-Villani conjecture|journal= Journal of Statistical Physics|volume=115|issue=1–2|pages=185–190|year=2004|doi=10.1023/B:JOSS.0000019811.15510.27|bibcode=2004JSP...115..185L|arxiv=math-ph/0210027}}</ref> In 2015, [[Alexandre Eremenko]] gave a simplified proof of Stahl's theorem.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Eremenko, A. È.|title=Herbert Stahl's proof of the BMV conjecture|journal=Sbornik: Mathematics|volume=206|issue=1|year=2015|pages=87–92|doi=10.1070/SM2015v206n01ABEH004447|bibcode=2015SbMat.206...87E|arxiv=1312.6003}}</ref>

In 2023, [[Otte Heinävaara]] proved a structure theorem for [[Hermitian matrices]] introducing [[tracial joint spectral measures]] that implies Stahl's theorem as a corollary.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Heinävaara, Otte|title=Tracial joint spectral measures|date=2023 |class=math.FA |eprint=2310.03227}}</ref>

==Statement of the theorem==
Let <math>\operatorname{tr}</math> denote the [[Trace (linear algebra)|trace]] of a [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]]. If <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> are <math>n\times n</math> [[Hermitian matrix|Hermitian matrices]] and <math>B</math> is [[Positive semidefinite matrix|positive semidefinite]], define <math>\mathbf{f}(t) = \operatorname{tr}(\exp(A-tB))</math>, for all real <math>t\geq 0</math>. Then <math>\mathbf{f}</math> can be represented as the [[Laplace transform]] of a non-negative [[Borel measure]] <math>\mu</math> on <math>[0,\infty)</math>. In other words, for all real <math>t\geq 0</math>,
: <math>\mathbf{f}</math>({{math|t}}) = <math>\int_{[0,\infty)} e^{-ts}\, d\mu(s)</math>, 
for some non-negative measure <math>\mu</math> depending upon <math>A</math> and <math>B</math>.<ref name="Clivaz2016">{{cite book|last1=Clivaz|first1=Fabien|title=Stahl's Theorem (aka BMV Conjecture): Insights and Intuition on its Proof|volume=254|year=2016|pages=107–117|issn=0255-0156|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-29992-1_6|series=Operator Theory: Advances and Applications|isbn=978-3-319-29990-7 |arxiv=1702.06403}}</ref>
